chapter: West Coast trip and Mildred's circle
title: Mildred's glandular condition and weight
summary: Mildred was slim as a girl but gained weight from a glandular condition, which Norvo thinks may be why she had no children; none of her brothers had it.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Oh. Well listen, Red, I remember Mildred showing me a snapshot of her where she was a slender little thing.
Yeah.
Don't you remember seeing the picture?
Oh, sure. I remember that. Then she --
Well she must've had a glandular thing --
Yeah, she had a glandular condition, cause she gained weight after I knew her, too, you know?
Oh, did she?
Oh, yeah.
But -- but she was fairly -- put on a fair bit of weight when she was with Whiteman, though, hadn't she?
YEAH. That's when she was really putting it on.
She was putting it on.
But she'd gone to doctors and they didn't know too much in those days --
In those days, I guess they didn't. No.
-- too much about glandular conditions, yeah. And --
Well, when you first met her, was she -- was -- had she put on fair weight, when you first met her?
She was plump, then.
Yeah, yeah.
Yeah, she was plump.
Yeah.
And --
Are any of the boys -- did any of the boys have that condition?
No, never had that problem at all.
Isn't that rotten luck?
It was her glandular condition; (Unintelligible), none of the boys -- Al is very thin, Chuck's very thin --
Isn't that funny?
-- Miles' very thin, there none of them ever put on the weight.
Yeah, that's sad, isn't it, probably, you know, today, they probably would've made tests to know --
Course the doctor told her long ago that
she had that -- told her in California that she had a -- glandular problem.
Yeah. Well --
Probably that was the reason she never had children. Or something, I don't know.
Yeah.

They seemed to think so at the time. I know when we were in New York, here, she tried to -- she went to doctors who were supposed to be specialists and that, but it didn't -- it really was hit and miss I think.
Well I don't think even today it would -- Red -- in -- I don't think they know too much --
No, I mean --
-- there must a -- be a whole lot more that they could know that they don't know, you know --
Yeah.
-- well that's getting away from ourselves a little bit but --
Yeah.
-- but I just was interested in that background so --
